finding_dispositions.note: PL 9 PDF pp. 302-303 re-read at 300 dpi. scope.md 3.10 now marks the italic paragraph summaries (nos. 1, 2, 5, 6) as the Maurist editors' and quotes Hilary's own text: Salutaris enim noster Jesus est; Judicium post consummationem saeculi ... (Ps 1:5); Non illud utique ...; fieri judicium ab his qui se persequuntur ... Sunt enim spiritales nequitiae; conterat intra se diabolum; Lk 10:19. It labels his 'now' as drawn from the unsung v. 84a (and v. 83) and states how his comment bears on the sung v. 84b: persecutors = devil and ministers by Eph 6:12; the power to crush them; final judgment affirmed. The same applies in scope 4.4 (the time difference traced to each witness's reading of 84a), 1.3 table and 6. In interpretations.md: rules, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 anagogical (his own 'diabolum in resurrectionis saeculo judicandum'), 1.6, 3.3, 3.7, 4.2 persecutors row, 4.3 and 4.4. Bindings and verified.md were updated to match.

Theodoret's censure (Constantinople II, ratified by Vigilius, 553; his writings against St Cyril and Ephesus, one of the Three Chapters; CE 04308b; not his exegesis) is recorded in scope 3.5, 3.10 and the section 6 register. His role is now structural and contextual only (the Ps 89 title opinions; the literal setting of Ps 118:83-84), and the binding role is changed to context. 'Greek tradition' and 'direct' are removed, and interpretations 3.7, 4.4 and 5 no longer present him as a reception witness. As the alternative, the PG 27 expositions printed under Athanasius's name were read on IA page renditions (n204, n253, n254), Greek and Latin (Ps 89 title and vv. 1-2; Ps 118:81, 84a, 86b). They were recorded under the printed attribution as contributing, with no reading carried. The 5.2 bound states that no Greek witness of registered standing and unquestioned authorship was read on Ps 89:1-2 or Ps 118:81-86.

summary: Repaired both research findings. Hilary's Caph on the PL 9 page images now carries only his own words, with the Maurist italic summaries labelled as the editors'; the record states that his present-not-final judgment rests on the unsung v. 84a and Ps 1:5, and how his comment bears on the sung v. 84b. Theodoret's censure is recorded and he is restated as context only. The PG 27 Psalm expositions printed under Athanasius's name were read on page images for Ps 89 and Ps 118:81-86 and recorded with their attribution bound. Readings 1 and 3 and the 4.2-4.4 comparison were adjusted to match.
